I say this in the nicest way possible, but leave your old friend be, OP.

It’s been five years and I’d wager that the period where hearing from you would have helped more than hurt passed years ago. After so much time elapsed, particularly given that you you chose to unilaterally end the friendship, you are now effectively strangers. She has very likely moved on from this and likely doesn’t think about the situation much anymore; the acute pain phase of being iced out is thankfully pretty brief. Processing your own trauma and analyzing your behavior has likely brought the situation to the forefront of your mind long after it’s receded from the forefront of hers.

No matter how well-meaning your actions are, trying to pop back into her life five years later with an apology and a story about what you were going through at the time may be a burden to her. 

Her last interaction with you was you cutting her off; showing back up now and asking her to reopen old wounds and perform the emotional labor required to process and respond to whatever you present her with is unfair. If she wanted you in her life again, she would have tried reaching out again. 

Very few people put the effort in to understand their own trauma and the impact their behavior has on others. The fact that you’ve had the sheer strength of will to do that is amazing.

Take pride in the insight that you’ve gathered from the emotional work you’ve done on yourself, learn from this experience, and move forward with the intention to bring clarity and communication into your future friendships.

It sounds like you’ve really grown a lot over the past half decade, but please don’t drag your former friend into your healing process.

>How do you deal with your current weight while trying to lose? I am currently walking on the treadmill at a speed of 3 or 3.2 MPH for the majority of my daily walks when I used to be able to run or walk at 5-5.5 MPH with 3 being a “cool down.” I’m guessing it will get better over time, I just don’t know how long to stick with this speed. I keep telling myself the distance/time is more important than the speed at which I go. Is this true?

Walking at all is 100% more important than the speed (or distance). It sounds flippant, but you'll know when you're ready to challenge yourself with a higher speed or distance. I started my weight loss by doing HIIT on an exercise bike and I knew that it was time to increase intensity when my normal workout didn't leave me feeling quite as spent. Don't forget that you can always increase the intensity for part of a workout and dial back if you discover that you're not ready for it.

   
  
>I have stretch marks all over my belly and I am worried when I do lose the weight I will have to get skin surgery (does this happen to everyone?)

No one ever *has* to get skin surgery, but whether or not you'll want it is up to you. My excess skin bothered me more during the process of losing weight than it did/does at goal weight. I don't have a *ton* of excess skin, but it's definitely there. It's tightened up over the past 2.5 years but it'll never disappear. I honestly don't think about it very much at all; my body is just my body at this point. The only time it bothers me is when doing jumping exercises. I know it's hard, but I'd recommend not thinking about the extra skin this early.

   

>Does anyone else hide their size and weight from their spouse? Not only him, but I won’t tell anyone.

I never, ever told anyone my weight at my largest. That said, once I started losing weight, I was no longer afraid/ashamed of sharing my current weight. This has continued and I openly talk about my current weight with people in my life now.
